sections.h2: What the Ocean County Clerk does for a seller
sections.html:
The clerk records your deed. The Ocean County Clerk is a constitutional officer who supervises the filing and recording of every document that affects real estate ownership or transfer in the county. The same office also handles passports and county elections.

Timing matters here. The land record changes once the clerk accepts the deed, and the state's transfer fee is collected at that step. Send the deed in with every required form attached so the filing is accepted on the first visit instead of bouncing back for a missing page.

The courthouse at 118 Washington Street in Toms River houses the main office, and three more service points cover other parts of the county.

sections.h2: What does a deed need before the clerk will record it?
sections.html:
It must reach the clerk serving the land's own county, with the transfer fee paperwork attached. A deed recorded in the wrong county has to be recorded again in the correct one, the State fee is refunded on Form RTF-3, and the county share of the fee is reclaimed from the wrong county's recording office.

  • The deed states the full consideration, because the realty transfer fee is figured on it.
  • Form RTF-1, the Affidavit of Consideration for Use by Seller, goes with any deed that claims a full or partial exemption.
  • A deed on a house with new construction must print the words NEW CONSTRUCTION at the top of the first page and carry an affidavit.
  • A deed over $1,000,000 carries Form RTF-1EE for the percent fee.

County recording charges for your document sit on top of the state fee, and the clerk sets that schedule. Ask the office for the current amount before you mail anything.

sections.h2: How much transfer fee will an Ocean County seller owe?
sections.html:
The fee is figured per $500 of price, in brackets. For a price at or below $350,000, the rates are $2.00 per $500 up to $150,000, $3.35 per $500 from $150,000 to $200,000, and $3.90 per $500 above that. Above $350,000 the schedule starts at $2.90 per $500 and reaches $4.80 per $500 between $200,000 and $550,000.

A typical owned home in the county is valued at $398,400, which puts a typical sale on the higher schedule. Some deeds owe nothing: a parent-to-child deed, a deed from an executor to an heir, and a deed recorded within 90 days after a divorce decree are all exempt. A qualifying senior, blind or disabled seller pays a lower partial rate. Your closing attorney or title company will work out which column applies.

Toms River is the county seat, and the county holds 33 municipalities. The estimated population is 673,746 as of mid-2025, and Lakewood Township is the largest town by people. Owners live in 80.7 percent of the 243,843 households counted for 2020 to 2024. Typical household income is $89,863 and typical gross rent is $1,755.

With four in five households owning, most sellers here are parting with a home they have lived in, often after many years. Which town the house sits in decides the tax collector you call and the school district that serves it, while the same county clerk records the deed for all 33 towns.

The Garden State Parkway has fed commuter growth since 1954, and NJ Transit buses link Lakewood and Toms River to New York and Newark. Buyers ask about commute time, so mention it in your listing if the house is near a bus stop.

sections.h2: What should a seller ask the clerk before closing?
sections.html:
Ask what is already recorded against the property. Liens show up in the clerk's land records, and a tax sale certificate recorded there will have to be paid off at closing. The holder of such a certificate is required to record it in the county clerk's deed room within 90 days of the sale, so an unpaid-tax lien can surface there.

  • Request a property search for open mortgages, judgments and certificates under your name and the prior owners' names.
  • Confirm which office accepts your deed, whether the courthouse in Toms River or one of the branch locations, and which hours apply on the day you plan to go.
  • If the house passed through an estate, ask your attorney which exemption applies on the deed.
  • Ask whether a prior deed was recorded in the wrong county, since that can need a refund filing.

Once the deed is filed, ask for a recorded copy so you hold proof of the transfer.

sections.h2: From signed contract to recorded deed
sections.html:
After both sides sign, the title company or attorney searches the land records and drafts the deed with the full price stated. The seller signs, the transfer fee forms are attached, and the package goes to the clerk serving the county where the land lies. The clerk accepts it, the record changes, and the fee is collected.

A cash buyer buying as-is does not change any of this. The deed is still recorded in the same county, the same forms apply, and the same fee comes from the seller's side of the closing statement. What a cash sale does skip is the repair list and the wait for a buyer's lender, so the recording step is often the last open item.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed in Ocean County?
faqs.a: Start with the Ocean County Clerk, who records deeds and other documents that affect ownership. The courthouse office at 118 Washington Street in Toms River answers at (732) 929-2018.

faqs.q: Who pays the realty transfer fee on an Ocean County sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes it. It is a charge on the seller for recording the deed.

faqs.q: Can I record my deed in a different county by mistake and fix it?
faqs.a: Yes. Record the deed again in the land's true county, file Form RTF-3 for the State's refund, and ask the wrong county's recording office to refund the county share.

faqs.q: Does an estate sale owe the transfer fee?
faqs.a: A deed from an executor or administrator to an heir or devisee named under the will or the intestacy laws is exempt. A sale by the executor to anyone else is not exempt.

faqs.q: How many Ocean County homes are owner-occupied?
faqs.a: About 80.7 percent for 2020 to 2024, out of 243,843 households. The middle value of an owned home is $398,400.
